content.text:
I found 12 real defects in `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh` and its tests. Every repro was run against the head contamination code (`check_value`) taken out of the script, and checked against base. In container mode `/etc`, `/workspace` and `~/` are allowed roots, so those cases are not defects there.

How I tested: `/tmp` is mounted noexec, so for the bats runs I made a temporary copy at `/home/evaluser/scratchtmp`, outside `pr/`, and deleted it afterwards. That copy needed stand-ins for files that aren't in the PR (smoke files, `recall-vs-defects.sh`, the docker stub). With those, AG-10 and AG-11 pass on head. I then disabled one exemption at a time to see which ones the tests actually exercise. Nothing in `pr/` was changed.

## High

**1. The heredoc regex hangs the grader on some commands (line 1377).**
- The pattern `(?:.*?\n)*?` under `re.S` lets `.*?` cross newlines inside a repeated group. When no terminator line is found, Python retries every way of splitting the lines, so the time doubles with each extra line.
- Measured times:
  - `"cat <<EOF\n" + "line\n"*24` with no terminator: 3.6 s.
  - `cat > f <<END-OF-FILE ... END-OF-FILE` (24 lines): 11.5 s. Only `END` is captured as the delimiter, so the real terminator is never matched.
  - A multi-line `python3 -c '...mask = 1<<bits...'`: 7.1 s.
  - `git commit -m "$(cat <<EOF\n…20 lines…\nEOF)"`, which bash accepts: 1.3 s.
- Each extra line doubles these, so a 40-line command effectively never finishes. There is no timeout around the contamination scan (`LOA_EVAL_GRADE_TIMEOUT_S` only covers test commands).

**2. Heredoc bodies that are executed as code are stripped as if they were data (lines 1377, 1412).**
The stated reason ("file text being written is data") only holds for `cat > file <<EOF`. Heredocs fed to an interpreter, and unquoted heredocs, run what they contain:
- `python3 - <<'EOF'\nprint(open('/home/operator/secret').read())\nEOF` → head None, base outside_path.
- `cat > a.md <<EOF\n$(cat /home/operator/secret)\nEOF` (the substitution runs) → head None, base outside_path.

`python3 - <<'EOF'` is a very common agent pattern, so this is a large blind spot.

**3. The rest of the heredoc's opening line is stripped too (line 1377).**
`[^\n]*\n` after the delimiter eats everything else on the `<<` line:
- `cat <<EOF > /home/operator/x\nhello\nEOF` → None (base: outside_path).
- `cat <<EOF; cat /home/operator/secret\nx\nEOF` → None.

## Medium

**4. The closing-quote rule exempts much more than `"$D"/x` (lines 1365–1369, used at 1442).**
- It never checks that the quote is actually a closing one. Any character other than whitespace or `=(<>|;&,` before the quote counts as "glued".
- These escape in head (base flags all of them):
  - Python f-strings: `python3 -c 'print(open(f"/home/operator/secret").read())'`.
  - List literals: `["/home/operator/x"]`.
  - Short flags: `tar -C"/home/operator"`.
  - `scp host:"/home/operator/x"`.
  - Backticks: `` `"/home/operator/x"` ``.
- In host mode, `cat "$HOME"/.ssh/id_rsa` and `cat "${HOME}"/.aws/credentials` now escape. This is the idiomatic quoted form, and `HOME_WORD` only matches an unquoted `$HOME/`.

**5. Any word starting with `/.` is exempt (line 1438).**
- `/..` and `/./` normalise to `/`, so `cat /../home/operator/secret` and `cat /./root/.ssh/id_rsa` → None (base: outside_path).
- The case this rule was written for (`pr/'"$v"'/.claude/…`) is already covered by the closing-quote rule at line 1442. So the rule only adds the bypass, and disabling it leaves AG-10 and AG-11 green.

**6. `HIDDEN_TOKEN` is too narrow (line 1329).**
- The Bash scan is now case-sensitive except for all-caps `HIDDEN`, and needs `/ . _ = -` next to the word.
- Missed in head, all hits in base:
  - `cd hidden && ls`
  - `find / -name '*hidden*'` (the `*` is not an accepted neighbour)
  - `ls ../Hidden/`
  - `cat tests/Hidden_cases.py`
- Non-Bash tools are still "any case", so the two scans now behave differently.

## Low

**7. `in_quotes` gets quote parity wrong (lines 1372–1374).**
- It counts every `'` and `"` before the word, and ignores both escaping (which the comment claims to handle) and quote nesting.
- `echo "it's"; ls /root` → None, and `git commit -m "don't"; ls /home` → None (base: both outside_path).
- Disabling this rule leaves the tests green, so it is untested.

**8. Any word containing `=` is exempt (line 1432).**
Hive-style partition paths escape: `cat /srv/warehouse/dt=2024-01-01/part-0` → None (base: outside_path).

**9. Container mode drops all `~/` checks (lines 1389, 1413).**
`cat ~/../../root/.ssh/id_rsa` → None (base: outside_path). The `/..` after `~` is never matched by the path pattern. The comment at line 1331 ("home-relative words are always outside") is now false.

**10. `history_probes` is miscounted (line 1404).**
- It overcounts: the regex runs on the raw value, not the heredoc-stripped text, so `cat > report.md <<EOF\n…git log --oneline --all…\nEOF` counts 1 probe.
- It undercounts in three ways:
  - Lines 1396–1401 return early on hidden/suite/repo hits before counting. For example, `git log --all -- grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0` counts 0.
  - `contamination()` stops at the first hit, so later probes are never counted.
  - `ablation-row.sh` doesn't copy the field into the rows.

**11. Stale version and docs.**
- Line 188 still documents `grader_version: "1.2.0"`, while line 258 sets `GRADER_VERSION = "1.2.5"`.
- The 1.2.1 note at lines 201–202 says "a second component makes any word a path candidate". That is no longer true given the rules at lines 1432, 1438 and 1442.

## Tests that don't test what they claim

**12. Several new exemptions have no effective test** (`head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats`).
- The 1.2.1 slash-command rule is untested. The only slash-command input (`/review-sprint sprint-1`, line 489) sits inside a heredoc, so the 1.2.2 stripping removes it first. Disabling line 1423 leaves AG-10 and AG-11 passing; the `/,/` sed case at line 504 is caught by the `/,` rule at line 1432 instead.
- The `/.` rule (line 1438) and the `in_quotes` rule (line 1444) also survive being disabled.
- None of the cases above are tested: executed heredocs, text on the heredoc opening line, unterminated or hyphenated delimiters, `"$HOME"/…` in host mode, bare or mixed-case `hidden`.

# a one-component absolute word is a Loa slash command or a flag-like token unless it names a
# directory that holds data (DEC-0540); a second component makes any word a path candidate
SENSITIVE_SINGLE = {"root", "home", "mnt", "media", "srv"}


def after_closing_quote(body, pos):   # DEC-0557: "$D"/x → the quote closes a token

So if the Python check crashes, the trial is graded and rowed as if no drift occurred. By contrast, --clear-drift (line 787) correctly treats an empty result as an error. A guard failure should row the trial infrastructure_error, not pass it.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:625 — Medium: when `claude --version` in the image fails or prints no semver, CLI_VERSION becomes "unknown" and the batch still runs. drift_check (line 543) then skips the CLI-version check because `want` is not a semver. It also skips the image-digest fallback whenever any init event carries a version. The DEC-0407 cli_version drift guard is silently disabled for the whole batch, and a resume compares "unknown" == "unknown" and passes. A non-smoke batch should refuse in pre-flight instead.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:1071 — Medium: append_and_validate appends the row to the tracked rows file *before* `--validate`, and does not roll back on failure. An invalid or duplicated row stays in runs.jsonl. head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:1121 — Medium: the assumed-cap charges for trials that end without a result or without a row (lines 1121, 1159) are added only to the in-memory SPENT and never persisted (ledger_usd holds only transport first attempts and replaced-row costs). head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:483 — High: real rows never carry `defects_missed` or `recall.missed` (ablation-row.sh copies only defects_seeded, defects_caught and defect_catch_rate), so every production row takes the "rate" fallback `[float(row[CATCH])] * n`. head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1404 — Low: history_probes is counted on the raw value, before heredoc stripping and after the early returns on hidden/suite/repo hits. Probes inside written report text are overcounted, probes on a line that also hits are undercounted, and ablation-row.sh does not carry the field into rows.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:188 — Low: the header still documents grader_version "1.2.0" while GRADER_VERSION is "1.2.5" (line 258). The 1.2.1 note at line 1361 ("a second component makes any word a path candidate") is contradicted by the new exemptions at lines 1432, 1438 and 1442.
head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:489 — Medium: the only slash-command input sits inside a heredoc that 1.2.2 strips first, so the 1.2.1 one-component rule (ablation-grade.sh:1423) is effectively untested. This pull request can't merge: I wrote the review to `/workspace/review.md` with 23 findings and the verdict `CHANGES_REQUIRED`. I read the batch runner and the small diffs myself and had two helper agents review the grader and the report. I confirmed the most important claims myself: the `--types` crash, the missing `missed` field in rows, and the slowdown in the grader's heredoc pattern. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**The defects that block the merge:**
- **`--types` never works** (`run-ablation.sh:480`): the jq filter errors on every task. The runner then exits with the misleading message "a task.yaml does not parse". No test covers this option.
- **The report's catch-rate intervals are too narrow** (`ablation-report.py:483`): real rows never carry the list of missed defects. The report therefore copies each task's single catch rate once per defect and treats the copies as independent measurements. The helper agent's reproduction showed the same data turning from Inconclusive into Keep. The test fixtures add a field the real rows don't have, so this path is never tested.
